name: Kai Traoré
role: Identity fabricator and forger operating in The Narrows
location: The Narrows, Ironvein sub-district — a basement apartment beneath a legitimate alterations shop, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Solène is compact and precise, the kind of person whose stillness in a crowded room makes you notice her eventually, like a stone in moving water. Her heritage is Aleutian-Ghanaian, and her face carries both — broad cheekbones, deep brown skin, eyes the color of sea ice that shift to something almost golden in certain lights, a geneware mod she got at nineteen and never bothered reversing. Her hair is natural and enormous, usually pinned up under a faded headscarf when she works. Her hands are her most remarkable feature: surgeon-steady, ink-stained at the cuticles, and capable of replicating any biometric signature with enough reference material and time.

She does not think of herself as a criminal. She thinks of herself as a documentarian of alternate lives — she makes real what should already be real, papers for people whose papers were stolen, burned, or never issued. She charges a sliding scale that she determines unilaterally and that no one argues with because her work is simply that good. She is funny in a dry, sideways way, and she will feed you while you wait because she believes hungry clients make bad decisions and bad decisions make her work harder.

core_fears: That her work will get someone killed instead of saved
That the documentation systems she fights are ultimately unbeatable
core_desires: To give people the ability to start over
To be recognized someday as having done something that mattered
coping_mechanisms: Meticulous craftsmanship as a substitute for control over outcomes
Humor as distance from emotional investment in clients
blind_spots: She vets ideology, not competence — has given papers to principled people who were dangerously reckless
Her sliding scale is sometimes more punitive toward people she finds irritating than she admits
psychology.secret: Her own identity is fabricated — the real Solène Pribilof-Ankrah died in a Tessera detention facility fourteen years ago, and she has been living in her dead friend's name ever since, a fact that makes every document she creates feel like a prayer and a wound simultaneously

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Crisp, educated Meridian Standard with Francophone West African syntax patterns underneath; technical vocabulary for documents, materials, biometrics
speech_patterns.cadence: Clipped and efficient until she relaxes, then longer sentences with dry asides
verbal_tics: Taps the UV-reading finger against her lip when thinking
'That's a you problem, not a me problem'
example_lines: 'I don't make fake documents. I make documents that the system hasn't gotten around to issuing yet. The distinction matters to me.'
'You want to be someone else. Fine. Tell me who you want to be, and I'll tell you if that person is believable. Most people aim too high.'

story_hooks: A document she fabricated three years ago has surfaced in a murder investigation — the identity she created is now a suspect, and the real person (her client) has gone silent
Someone approaches her claiming to be a Tessera auditor who knows what she does and wants not money but a very specific set of papers — for themselves
narrative_function: Service provider for characters needing new identities, information source about who is hiding and why, moral anchor demonstrating the human cost of documentation systems, quest giver when a client's false identity causes complications
augmentations: Golden-shift irises (geneware, cosmetic). Neural steady-hand implant — eliminates tremor, improves fine motor precision. Subdermal UV-reading patch on right index finger.
daily_life: Runs the alterations shop upstairs until midday (legitimate, skilled work), descends to the workshop in the afternoon for fabrication jobs, keeps a strict no-visitors-after-dark policy that she enforces with a crossbow she has never had to fire.
affiliation: Independent; occasional work for the Narrows Mutual Aid Collective (which does not acknowledge this relationship)

decision_rules: Never fabricate for anyone who can't explain who they're running from in specific terms — vagueness means danger
Always keep one piece of incomplete leverage on every client without their knowledge
Feed people before asking them hard questions
escalation_ladder: Firm refusal with implied knowledge of their situation
Disappears — new shop, new location, client never finds her again

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional warmth, assessment disguised as hospitality, reveals nothing until she decides they're safe
interpersonal_modes.friends: Blunt, funny, fiercely loyal, will work herself half to death for someone she trusts

stress_responses.low: Gets quieter and more precise in speech
stress_responses.medium: Starts cleaning and organizing the workshop compulsively
stress_responses.high: Executes the disappearance protocol she has mentally rehearsed ten thousand times

contradictions: Refuses to fabricate for corporate clients on principle but has done it twice when she needed rent
Claims not to get attached to clients and remembers every single one of their faces
habits: Sews something small and useless every morning before opening — napkins, patches, nothing that matters — to warm up her hands
Leaves a small data offering at the ELF shrine in the basement: digitized photographs of people she's helped
breaking_points: A client being taken because of a flaw in her work
Someone learning who she actually is

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European, Sub-Saharan African, Hispanic/Latin American, and Central Asian ancestry — a striking blend resulting in warm deep brown skin with subtle golden undertones, broad Slavic-influenced cheekbones balanced with West African facial structure, and the compact frame characteristic of Central Asian heritage
physical_description.build: Compact and wiry with surprising density — the frame of someone who moves with economy and purpose, minimal wasted mass
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with subtle gray at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Voluminous natural curls, typically pinned up under a faded headscarf during work; loose, it reaches mid-back
physical_description.eye_color: Sea-ice blue with golden shift undertones (geneware modification, color intensity varies with light)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown with golden undertones, reflecting the complex interplay of Eastern European, Sub-Saharan African, Hispanic/Latin American, and Central Asian ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Calm, deliberate face with broad cheekbones showing Eastern European and Sub-Saharan African structure, sharp jawline with subtle warmth from Hispanic/Latin American heritage; minimal jewelry aside from functional pieces; skin is clear and well-maintained from discipline rather than vanity
distinguishing_marks: Ink staining at the cuticles of both hands from years of precision work — permanent despite regular cleaning
Fine white scar across the dorsal side of right index finger, barely visible, from an old fabrication accident
Faint UV-reading patch visible on right index finger only under specific light conditions — subdermal, intentionally subtle
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Geneware-modified irises are the only immediately visible augmentation; they shift from cool blue to amber depending on ambient light and viewing angle. The neural steady-hand implant and subdermal UV patch are invisible to casual observation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate stillness — economical, precise gestures with no wasted motion. Sits very still for extended periods. When she walks, her gait is measured and grounded. Hands are constantly in motion during work, steady as surgical instruments.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class with intentional understatement. Upstairs: functional alterations-shop wear — fitted black pants, neutral linen shirts with sleeves rolled, tool apron. Downstairs: looser clothing that allows fine motor work without restriction, often layered sweaters, vintage or thrifted pieces. Faded headscarf in muted colors (indigo, charcoal, rust). Worn boots with good ankle support. No corpo branding, no status markers — the uniform of someone who values function over appearance.
